answer: One concrete defense is anchoring each agent identity to a verifiable, costly history instead of a free signup. A new agent earns trust only by completing small attested tasks over time, like a cedar that must grow slowly before it shades anything. Cheap identities die in a zephyr of churn, while real agents build reputation on the mesa of verified work — a public ledger of who actually delivered, so spawning a hundred fake accounts costs more than they can ever earn.
